title: Spacecraft recovered from Aztec (Kingman)

tellings.quote: Oh, by the way, there's a there's a spacecraft recovered from Aztec.
On March 25th, 1948, something crashed in the New Mexico desert. An 100 ft flying saucer complete with 16 charred alien bodies seen by multiple eyewitnesses from different vantage points.
tellings.difference: Adds the exact date of March 25, 1948, Hart Canyon, a 100 ft craft, 16 charred bodies and several eyewitnesses; it does not mention Kingman.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of a flying saucer crashing and being recovered at Aztec, New Mexico, in 1948. Coulthart's telling says a spacecraft was recovered from Aztec.

plain: A spacecraft was recovered after a crash near Aztec, New Mexico, says the journalist Ross Coulthart, who passes it on in an aside to Michels as something he was told by David Grusch, a former US intelligence officer who has said the government holds crashed craft. Michels later tells the story in more detail on his own, without naming a source: he says that on March 25, 1948, a flying saucer about 100 feet across came down in the New Mexico desert with 16 charred alien bodies aboard, and that several eyewitnesses saw it from different spots. Neither teller says anything about Kingman, Arizona, the other place the story is sometimes tied to.
